cards.source_title: AI That Works #5: Designing Evals (session notes)
cards.quote: don't use numbers for confidence, use a rubric
cards.claim: Grade with categorical, enum-based rubrics (for example slow / medium / fast) instead of numeric confidence scores.
cards.evidence: One bullet in the episode README; no data, no worked comparison. The page also lists LLM-as-judge and rubric design as topics without detail.
cards.first_guess: Confirms the section 5 habit of verdict and severity enums. Check whether any contract still carries a numeric confidence or score field and, if so, swap it for an enum whose levels the brief defines. Confirmation, not a change.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #5: Designing Evals (session notes)
cards.quote: capture intermediate steps of your pipeline as probes and individual testable components
cards.claim: Start with vibe evals (run the prompt, look at the output), add a few passing cases and end-to-end tests, treat each pipeline stage as a probe, and grow a golden dataset from production data while reviewing diffs of both raw and structured output.
cards.evidence: README bullets only, no numbers or case study. The MLOps Community mini-summit talk (2025-04-17, read) makes the same point as a 'data flywheel' that turns production failures into test cases, again without data.
cards.first_guess: Each Workflow stage already returns a validated StructuredOutput object, which is a ready-made probe. Saving the brief plus the accepted object from past runs gives a golden set for free. A brief test would be: replay the brief, diff the structured objects field by field. Start with verdict and severity fields only.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #67: Your Model is Already Obsolete (README of the harness)
cards.quote: A broken eval is worse than no eval.
cards.claim: A test harness for model swaps needs its own safeguards: refuse to judge when an input (price) is missing, repeat runs because single runs mislead, and check that assertions can actually pass.
cards.evidence: README lists the author's own run: a missing price defaulted to zero and silently passed four of five candidates; single-run evals gave two confidently wrong answers so it now runs three repeats; a BAML assertion that is always false sent the optimizer chasing an unsatisfiable test. Small, self-reported, not independent. In the transcript Vaibhav does not speak (Kevin and Dex do).
cards.first_guess: Three cheap rules for any future brief-test spec: include a deliberately failing case that must fail, return 'cannot judge' instead of defaulting a missing input, and run each case more than once because agent output varies. No code to adopt.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #67: Your Model is Already Obsolete (transcript and README)
cards.quote: The regression budget is something you drag, not something you set once.
cards.claim: Evaluate a swapped model by diffing its structured output against the incumbent's on the same cases, with no hand-labelled set. Send disagreements to a human, then into the golden set. Gate on a relative budget (accuracy no worse, cost and p95 latency within multiples).
cards.evidence: README quote is verbatim. The diff-against-incumbent and disagreements-to-human claims come from Kevin and Dex in an auto-generated transcript, read through a fetch extractor. Budget thresholds (1.2x cost, 1.5x p95) are illustrative demo values, not results.
cards.first_guess: A way to check the tier split (Sonnet research vs Opus verify): replay one lane's brief on both tiers, diff the cards, hand-label only the disagreements. A one-off check, not a standing gate.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #36: Building a Prompt Optimizer (live demo with a BAML team guest)
cards.quote: we only let you change the prompts and metadata on the types
cards.claim: BAML's optimizer reuses the existing test suite as its metric (default: fraction of tests passing), edits prompts by replacing the AST, and keeps the schema frozen so generated clients stay stable. It overfits if samples are unrepresentative, so a human still reads the result. Soft 'checks' grade without hard-failing a test.
cards.evidence: Live-demo transcript (auto-generated, read through a fetch extractor; quote may be lightly garbled). README gives no results. The README's 'constrained ways to edit specific parts of prompts' line is verbatim.
cards.first_guess: Principle only: if a brief is ever machine-edited, let it change prose and freeze the section 5 output contract, so downstream code never sees a shape change. Do not adopt GEPA or baml-py. Pairs with T-03 on trusting the metric.

cards.source_title: AI Engineer World's Fair 2026: fighting slop with slop (Vaibhav Gupta)
cards.source_date: 2026 (event year only; month not shown on page)
cards.quote: Inspect the transcript for incorrect behavior and unnecessary work,
cards.claim: Test a tool by having an agent use it from scratch, preserve the full transcript, have other agents inspect the transcript for wrong behaviour and wasted calls, let humans triage real problems from hallucinated ones, then let agents fix the confirmed ones. Run it on a schedule.
cards.evidence: Chaptered summary of a 21-minute talk. Example given: three tool calls where one would do. No counts of issues found or fixed. The Software Factory episode (2026-06-23, README read) adds deduplication across runs, a ticket with repro, a PR loop capped by max turns, and a nightly schedule; also unquantified.
cards.first_guess: The harness already keeps Workflow transcripts. An Opus pass that reads one lane's transcript for wasted fetches or ignored rules, with Fable or the owner triaging proposed brief edits, would improve briefs without writing tests. Keep the human triage step.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #63: Software Factory for Agent Tools
cards.quote: The shortest skill often beats the longest one
cards.claim: Run the same tasks against several versions of the instructions given to agents (an 'arena') and compare cost, turns and success. The shortest version often won.
cards.evidence: README states the arena and the result but gives no counts. The win is attributed to a runtime command (baml describe) supplying detail on demand, which our agents lack. The Anthropic post-mortem episode with Aaron (2025-10-07) separately asserts 'Use less context. I promise you, your pipelines will be more accurate.' with no data.
cards.first_guess: Brief and CONTEXT-block length is untested here. A small arena (same task, long vs trimmed CONTEXT, compare turns, cost and card quality) would turn a folk claim into data. Expect weaker transfer, since the cited win depended on a tool we do not have.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #34: Multimodal Evals (receipt extraction with BAML and Gemini)
cards.quote: deterministic checks that validate LLM outputs without using another LLM as a judge
cards.claim: Prefer deterministic cross-field checks (totals add up, values non-negative, required fields present) over an LLM judge. Judges double cost, vary between runs and are circular. On a failed check, re-extract.
cards.evidence: Demo project on the CORD-v2 receipt set with six checks and a dashboard; the README reports no accuracy numbers. Gupta's 2025-04-17 MLOps talk makes the same point in words ('I don't even need to ask another LLM'), also unquantified.
cards.first_guess: Workflow scripts are plain JS, so checks on the returned object are free: each quote is 15 words or fewer, each could_not_read url appears in urls_attempted, ids are unique, read_or_summarised is consistent with the source type. A failed check triggers one bounded retry that names the check. This is the most directly usable idea in the lane.

cards.source_title: The Data Exchange: Unleashing the Power of BAML in LLM Applications (show notes)
cards.quote: the model still outputs data matching your receipt schema, effectively hallucinating.
cards.claim: Forcing output into a schema can make a model fabricate a conforming answer for the wrong input. BAML instead lets the model reason freely and aligns the output afterwards. The 2025-06-10 'Cracking the Prompting Interview' notes add: give an 'Other' or 'Unknown' escape hatch.
cards.evidence: Vendor-side interview. The host discloses he is an investor in and advisor to Boundary. The receipt example is a story, not a measurement. The escape-hatch bullet is verbatim from the episode README: 'include an "Other" or "Unknown" category'.
cards.first_guess: Supports the honest-empty rule. Audit the contracts for required fields with no null path (for example source_date or quote on a summarised card), because those invite invention. Define an explicit 'unknown' convention in the contract. Claude's StructuredOutput is tool-call JSON rather than constrained decoding, so treat this as pressure from required fields, not a proven failure.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #9: Cracking the Prompting Interview (README)
cards.quote: Provide content with simple IDs (e.g., [SOURCE_1]) and have the LLM output these IDs.
cards.claim: Have the model emit short ids for sources, turns and categories and map them back to URLs or quotes in code. This improves accuracy and cuts tokens.
cards.evidence: README bullet with a small JSON example (dialogue_idx / speaker); no measurement of the accuracy or token claim.
cards.first_guess: For verifier or skeptic steps where the script holds the evidence list, number the items and require verdicts to cite ids. The script maps ids to url and quote and rejects unknown ids, so a fabricated URL cannot appear in that step. It does not apply to research lanes, where the agent finds sources itself.

cards.source_title: The Data Exchange: Unleashing the Power of BAML in LLM Applications (show notes)
cards.quote: in under a millisecond without requiring another LLM call.
cards.claim: Schema-aligned parsing is a local post-hoc parser: it strips markdown, backticks and commentary, corrects errors, aligns to the declared type, and raises if it cannot. It also claims token savings (a case number: 13 tokens in JSON Schema vs 4 in BAML) and up to 98% lower cost. It checks shape, not truth.
cards.evidence: Company-reported figures in a vendor-friendly interview (host is an investor). The 98% figure comes from customers moving to a smaller model. Boundary's own function-calling post (read) says SAP beats native function calling on BFCL, but its results table did not load and it states benchmark caveats. The MLOps talk's 'perfect answer all the time' is unquantified.
cards.first_guess: Corrects a misconception: SAP solves malformed text output. Our scripts already force a StructuredOutput tool call whose validation and model retry happen at the tool layer, and Workflow scripts cannot import libraries. Nothing to adopt. SAP would not catch a wrong fact, so it does not replace the evidence-string checks.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #75: All About Jev (README and transcript)
cards.quote: Output tokens in Jev are free because they're literally only outputting one token.
cards.claim: For routing and classification, a one-token classifier that returns probabilities over enum choices can replace a text-generating LLM call. Test any LLM call that outputs a single word against it. Jev clients are defined from BAML types.
cards.evidence: README reports Rippling reaching 90% accuracy against a 50% LLM baseline at 8x speed, with no method shown. In the garbled transcript Vaibhav says he has not looked into how it works and that most systems do not fit this case. Jev is a separate product, not BAML core.
cards.first_guess: No action. FixFlow has no LLM features and the knowledge-store CLI has no model by design. If a product feature ever needs routing or classification (message triage, fault-code suggestion), this is a candidate approach to evaluate then. Product idea only.

cards.source_title: AI Engineer World's Fair 2026: fighting slop with slop (Vaibhav Gupta)
cards.source_date: 2026 (event year only; month not shown on page)
cards.quote: Freedom in tool choice rests on stability in architectural obligations.
cards.claim: Keep a small tool-agnostic file of durable architectural rules (architecture.md, not a model-specific file), and enforce package boundaries with executable CI checks. The team reports the architecture unchanged for three or four months.
cards.evidence: One team of about eight people, self-reported in a talk summary. No comparison against a control.
cards.first_guess: Mostly confirmation: CLAUDE.md invariants plus import-linter and ESLint no-restricted-imports already do this. The only new angle is keeping the invariants separate from model-specific instructions, which CLAUDE.md currently mixes. Low value.

cards.source_title: AI Engineer World's Fair 2026: fighting slop with slop (Vaibhav Gupta)
cards.source_date: 2026 (event year only; month not shown on page)
cards.quote: Code can be slop, writing cannot.
cards.claim: Hold design documents to a stricter standard than code, and require that a design doc is actually read before it ships. Producing ten design docs a day overwhelmed the team; reading capacity, not generation, became the limit.
cards.evidence: Talk anecdote (a 2 AM post drew three readers; 'we book a meeting just to read'). Numbers are stated by the speaker, not measured.
cards.first_guess: A caution for the ship plan and knowledge-store design docs: long agent-written documents bottleneck on the owner's reading. The owner critique rounds already act as the read gate; keep each review packet small. No change proposed.

cards.source_title: AI That Works #26: Anthropic Post Mortem (Vaibhav and Aaron)
cards.quote: 30 test cases is often the magic number for basic coverage
cards.claim: About 30 representative cases is a workable first eval size. Collect production data continuously and turn subsets into eval datasets. Detect silent failures by calculating checksums and validating structured outputs in code.
cards.evidence: README rule of thumb with no supporting data. This is the only episode in the lane that lists Aaron Villalpando as a participant. The README's date for the Anthropic incidents looks unreliable and is not relied on.
cards.first_guess: Gives a size for a first brief-test set: roughly 30 cases drawn from past accepted runs, not 30 per brief. Combine with T-02 for where the cases come from and T-08 for how to check them.

notes: The prior assessment holds: nothing here argues for adopting BAML; the usable value is in ideas (T-08, T-02, T-03, T-09). WebFetch returns small-model extractions, so quotes were re-verified by a second fetch where possible; transcripts are auto-generated and garbled. AIE 2025 talk, Latent Space, Weaviate and Hamel appearances were not found; Aaron has no solo talk, only T-15. SAP, BFCL and 98% cost figures are vendor-reported.
